title: Entry of the first spermatozoon raises the surface tension of the egg

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Entry of the first spermatozoon raises the surface tension of the egg

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because later spermatozoa fail to enter the egg after the first, an immediate consequence of sperm entry is an increase in the surface tension of the egg.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: other spermatozoa, subsequent to the first, fail to effect an entry, we may safely conclude that an immediate consequence of the entry of the spermatozoon is an increase in the surface-tension of the egg

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “Fertilisation and the pronuclei”. Scope: fertilisation of animal eggs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The temporal and causal prediction is clear, and existing fertilization imaging can test the sequence and some proxies. Direct resolution of surface tension as the cause needs matched mechanical measurements that are sparsely public.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure egg cortical tension immediately before and after first sperm fusion while recording polyspermy block, and manipulate tension independently. Support requires a rapid tension increase that is necessary or sufficient to prevent later sperm entry.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Direct tension measurements are rarely archived with fertilization movies.

Cortical granule exocytosis and membrane depolarization are alternative blocks to polyspermy.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.8
discriminating power: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Failure of later sperm is not itself a tension measurement, but tension, membrane potential and envelope elevation have all been recorded often enough to compile a partial test. The rivals make different predictions, so the inference from polyspermy block to surface tension is decidable where those series exist. They do not yet cover animal eggs at large, and they are not in one archive.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure egg cortical tension immediately before and after the first sperm enters, and record whether later sperm are excluded when tension is experimentally held flat. A prompt tension increase that is required for the block would support the claim; exclusion of later sperm by membrane potential or a fertilization envelope, with tension unchanged, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Species differ in which block acts first.

Tension time series at fertilization are in papers on a few model eggs.

The electrical fast block and the cortical-granule envelope are confounded with any tension change if they are not measured separately.
